story.title: A team-tailoring skill for the skills maintainers
story.source_text: Set up a new skill in this repo: `skills-maintainers-refinement`, the team-tailoring skill for the people who maintain this skills collection. It does not exist yet. It ships the refinery.yaml that the self-runs already use (story-refinery/evals/self-run/refinery.yaml), names the owners, the Definition of Done (selftest.py is the test command; there is no linter), the label policy (documentation, enabler), the markdown tracker, and the language (Dutch tickets are normal). Loaded alongside story-refinery whenever a story in this repo is refined, so that TLR001 passes and nobody re-derives the house rules per story. Out of scope: refining anything itself; changing story-refinery.
story.summary_human: This repo has no tailoring skill, so each self-run rebuilt the same refinery.yaml by hand and none could pass TLR001. Create skills-maintainers-refinement from the template story-refinery ships: the config that already works here, the owners, a one-rule DoD (selftest), the label policy, markdown tracker, Dutch tickets. Walking skeleton first - the directory, a frontmatter that story-refinery's gates accept - then the house rules, then the README row. Nothing in story-refinery changes.
story.technical_notes_human: Greenfield: nothing to cite, so conventions cite the template (`template:story-refinery/assets/templates/team-tailoring-skill.md`) and the contract (`reference:story-refinery/references/tailoring.md`). Reuse ruled out: no tailoring skill and no other refinery.yaml exist (see ruled_out). D1: copy `story-refinery/evals/self-run/refinery.yaml` rather than symlink it - the self-run config is an eval fixture and must stay frozen. D2: name `skills-maintainers-refinement` so `tailoring.source` is self-describing in TLR001 messages. The skeleton (S0) is the directory with a template-derived SKILL.md and the config; S1 fills the house rules; S2 the README row (`README.md:12`).

conventions.rule: A tailoring skill is a copy of the template with the placeholders removed; it does not restate story-refinery's method.
tailoring.source in refinery.yaml must equal the skill's name, and the bundle records it (TLR001).
Anything mechanical - DoD command, label rule, budget - lives in refinery.yaml, never only in prose (TLR002).
Skill frontmatter carries name and description; this repo's skills use metadata.invocation to say auto or user.

critics.attempted: Executed S0 in my head from the template: the placeholders are <team> and <Team> in name, description and the heading - the stop_and_ask covers a different set. Ran the four done_when: the TLR001-on-old-bundle check proves the config is read, the tailored copy proves the gate clears; both are binary. Asked whether S1 and S2 could start alongside S0 - neither can, there is no directory. Asked why S2 is separate: docs kind is mandated on contract change here by convention of this repo's README, and it touches a file S0/S1 do not.

Re-opened the template (exists, placeholders as claimed), tailoring.md 'Where a rule belongs' (says what conventions[2] claims), README.md:12 (the table header line), and re-ran the reuse search (no tailoring skill, one refinery.yaml under evals/self-run). The standard: citation is the docs page story-refinery's own frontmatter follows; it cannot be opened offline, so it is marked as the weakest citation.

findings.claim: The tailored-copy check writes to /tmp, and the brief never says the copy is throwaway.
findings.failure: An implementer commits /tmp/skl1-tailored.json's content back into the bundle, or worse edits the self-run bundle in place - the eval fixture changes.
findings.resolution: forbidden gains 'do not modify anything under story-refinery/'; the command writes to /tmp only and the non-goal records the re-stamp as a follow-up.

findings.claim: The `standard:` citation points at a web page that cannot be re-opened offline.
findings.failure: A later reader cannot verify the frontmatter rule and either trusts it or re-derives it.
findings.resolution: story-refinery/SKILL.md's own frontmatter is the local instance of the standard and is named in the citation; the page is the source, the file is the proof.

findings.claim: The boundary example greps for 'example mapping' and 'agent brief' but the template itself mentions both in its own 'do not restate' warning.
findings.failure: S1's grep returns 1 on an untouched template and the criterion reads as failed.
findings.resolution: S1's done_when greps case-insensitively for the terms *outside* the template's HTML comment - the implementer strips the comment block; recorded in S1's read_first as the reason.
